finalText:
Merge: make new commit, join two branch histories. Both parent commits kept. History show real shape — branches, merge point, all commits as happened. Non-destructive, safe.

Rebase: replay your commits one-by-one onto tip of another branch. History rewrite — commits get new hashes, linear line, no merge bump. Cleaner log, but rewrite = danger if branch shared/pushed already (others' history diverge, force-push needed).

When each:
- Feature branch, solo work, want clean linear log before merge into main → rebase (interactive rebase good for squash/cleanup too).
- Branch shared with others, already pushed, or want true history of collab → merge.
- Public/shared branch (main, release) → never rebase. Merge only.
- Local branch, not pushed yet → rebase freely, safe.

Rule of thumb: rebase private, merge public.
